request: Analyze GSE152347 for PMID 33513138 (Ablation of DNA-methyltransferase 3A in skeletal muscle does not affect energy metabolism or exercise capacity.): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.

final.assay: Total RNA-seq (TruSeq Stranded Total RNA, Ribo-Zero Gold), 75-bp PE, soleus muscle (S4.9.p1, S2.1.p1)
final.sample_inclusion: 12-week-old male and female WT (Dnmt3a flox/flox) and mD3AKO mice; RNA-seq on 'rest' (sham treadmill) and 60 min after a 30-min treadmill bout only (S4.3.p1); n = 5-7 per genotype x exercise group (FIG2)
final.primary_estimand: Main effect of acute exercise (60 min after 30-min treadmill run vs rest) on soleus gene expression, pooled over genotype and sex (S2.2.p2, S4.17.p1)
planned_contrasts: exercise main effect: 60 min post vs rest (S2.2.p2; paper: 1615 DEGs, FDR 5%)
genotype main effect: mD3AKO vs WT (S2.2.p2, S2.6.p1; paper: 56 DEGs, 43 up / 13 down)
genotype x exercise interaction (S2.2.p2; paper: 0 DEGs)
final.repeated_measure_unit: none (one soleus per mouse; independent animals)
final.normalization: not_reported in this article ('processed as previously described [34]', S4.11.p1); expression threshold leaves 17389 genes (S4.9.p1), rule not stated
final.paper_method: Differential expression for a main effect of genotype, a main effect of exercise and a genotype/exercise interaction (S4.17.p1); software and model details deferred to ref [34] (S4.11.p1), not reported here. Sex handling in the RNA-seq model not reported.

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: Paper-first: the RNA-seq arm (S4.3.p1) is soleus from 12-week mice at rest vs 60 min after 30-min treadmill running, in both genotypes and both sexes. S4.17.p1 says DE was tested for main effects of genotype and exercise plus their interaction, FDR < 5%. S2.2.p2 reports 1615 exercise DEGs, 56 genotype DEGs, 0 interaction DEGs. No fold-change cutoff is stated. The DE software is not named (ref [34]).

checks: metadata series_id = 'GSE152347,GSE152349'; paper data availability names SuperSeries GSE152349 (S4.16.p1)
25 soleus samples, C57BL/6 mice, Sex Male/Female, genotype WT/KO, timepoint Bas/60 match S4.3.p1 (rest and 60 min) and FIG2 n = 5-7 per group
data_processing: STAR to mm10 + GENCODE vM15 + featureCounts matches S4.11.p1 (GENCODE M15)
contact Lars Roed Ingerslev, Copenhagen (author lab)

ownership.reasoning: GSE152347 is the RNA-seq SubSeries of the paper's GSE152349; sample groups and processing match the paper.

Sex, genotype and exercise state are parsed from the title; they agree with characteristics Sex/genotype/timepoint. 'Bas' is the rested/sham group, '60' is 60 min post exercise (S4.3.p1).

final.analysis_type: two-group with additive covariates (factorial 2x2 plus sex)

candidates.reason_rejected: the paper models genotype as a main effect; leaving it and sex out inflates residual variance (sex separates samples on MDS, S2.2.p3)
the paper's estimand is the main effect over both genotypes; per-genotype contrasts are run as exploratory

design.reasoning: S4.17.p1: main effects of genotype and exercise plus interaction. The primary exercise estimand is the main effect, which the additive model ~ sex + geno + time estimates (the paper found no interaction). The interaction and per-genotype exercise contrasts come from one joint model. Sex is added because the MDS shows sex separation (S2.2.p3) and both sexes are in every genotype x time cell.

covariance.reasoning: One soleus per mouse; no repeated measures, so no blocking term. Genotype is a design factor of the paper (S4.17.p1). Sex is a biological covariate: both sexes appear in every genotype x exercise cell, so it is not confounded with exercise. No batch, cage or litter column is recorded.

paper_route.method: not_reported (ref [34]); main effects genotype and exercise + interaction
paper_route.reason: the article does not name the DE software

deviations: DE software chosen by the workflow (DESeq2) because the article does not name it
the paper's expression filter (17389 genes kept) is not specified; DESeq2 independent filtering used in the primary; a CPM >= 1 in >= 3 samples filter is run as sensitivity

method.reasoning: Raw featureCounts counts support a count model. The article does not name the package, so DESeq2 is used with the paper's model structure (main effects plus sex). The interaction is tested in a joint DESeq2 cell-means model with sex as covariate.

threshold.reasoning: S4.17.p1 and S2.2.p2: FDR < 5%, no fold-change cutoff.

caveats: DE package not named in the article; DESeq2 used
